status.en: 22 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 38% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 22 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 38 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Armed attackers killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians in two separate incidents in Oromia, while a drone strike in western Oromia killed two government civil servants. Senior Tigray Military Commander Major General Yohannes was captured near the Eritrean border. Ethiopia received delivery of 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets, with plans for S-400 air defenses, amid rising tensions with Eritrea. Over 35,000 Ethiopians have fled across the Kenya border, and up to 50,000 are reported to have fled into Kenya's Moyale County. The conflict produced 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bevæpnede angripere drepte minst 60 ortodokse kristne i to separate hendelser i Oromia, mens et droneangrep i vestlige Oromia drepte to sivile ansatte i staten. Den senior tigrayiske militærkommandanten major general Yohannes ble tatt til fange nær grensen mot Eritrea. Etiopia mottok levering av 12 russiske Su‑35 jagerfly, med planer om S‑400 luftforsvar, midt i økende spenninger med Eritrea. Over 35 000 etiopiere har flyktet over Kenyas grense, og opptil 50 000 skal ha flyktet inn i Kenyas Moyale fylke. Konflikten førte til 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
